title: Overview: user, Muse, Authorize, MCP server
lede: The whole idea in four boxes. The user asks Muse, Muse acts for the user, PingOne Authorize decides, and only then does the MCP server run the tool.

nodes.label: 2. Muse
sub: The personal agent. Signs Sam in at PingOne and acts for him.

nodes.label: 3. PingOne Authorize
sub: Checks the audience, that Muse is a registered actor, and that the tool is allowed.

nodes.label: 4. MCP server
sub: Runs the tool and returns 4,500 points, Gold.

steps.title: Ask
steps.what: Sam asks Muse for his airline points. Muse acts only when asked.
steps.why: The request starts with a person, never with the agent.

steps.title: Delegated token
steps.what: Muse signs Sam in at PingOne and gets a delegated token: Sam is the subject and Muse is the actor. It presents that token at the gateway, which asks PingOne Authorize.
steps.why: Authorize can see who is asking and on whose behalf.

steps.title: Allowed, run tool
steps.what: Authorize checks the audience, that Muse is a registered actor, and that this tool is allowed. Only then does the request reach the MCP server.
steps.why: Policy decides every tool call. Without the actor, the call is refused.

steps.title: Points back
steps.what: The MCP server runs the tool and returns the points and tier. Muse shows them to Sam.
steps.why: The answer exists only because every check passed.
